title: K-flat complexes; functors preserving K-flat quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure $(\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ whose tensor bifunctor is additive in each variable. Assume that $\mathcal C$ has countable coproducts, meaning colimits of diagrams indexed by countable discrete categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Use $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For complexes $P,Q$ define their direct-sum total tensor complex by
$$
(P\otimes Q)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes Q^q,
$$
with differential on the $(p,q)$ summand equal to $d_P^p\otimes\mathrm{id}_{Q^q}$ into the $(p+1,q)$ summand plus $(-1)^p\mathrm{id}_{P^p}\otimes d_Q^q$ into the $(p,q+1)$ summand. For morphisms $a:P\to P'$, $b:Q\to Q'$, the morphism $a\otimes b$ is induced on the $(p,q)$ summand by $a^p\otimes b^q$ into the $(p,q)$ summand. A complex $P$ is *K-flat* if both functors $P\otimes-$ and $-\otimes P$ send every quasi-isomorphism of complexes to a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. An additive functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ (additive on each group of morphisms), applied termwise to complexes and their morphisms, *preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms* if $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to P'$ with both $P$ and $P'$ K-flat. Every exact $F$ has this property; here exact means additive and preserving finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: The total tensor construction is well defined: for each $n$, the pairs $(p,q)$ with $p+q=n$ form a countable set, so the displayed coproduct exists by the assumed countable coproducts and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define the differential by its two specified components on each summand. Its square has pure terms $d_P^{p+1}d_P^p\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathrm{id}\otimes d_Q^{q+1}d_Q^q$, both zero, and mixed terms with coefficients $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$, which cancel. Thus it is a cochain complex as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The displayed maps $a\otimes b$ commute with these differentials because $a,b$ commute with the respective differentials; their identities and compositions hold on every summand. Fixing either factor therefore gives the two functors used in the definition. No associativity or preservation of infinite coproducts by tensoring is needed for this binary construction.

source.place: Statement, sentence 2: totalizing the termwise tensor product; explicit direct-sum construction and sign check supplied here

proof.text: Suppose $F$ is exact and let $s:K\to L$ be any quasi-isomorphism, without assuming K-flatness. The termwise images are complexes since additivity gives $F(0)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to this exact functor between abelian categories. For every $n$ it supplies natural isomorphisms $c_K^n:H^n(FK)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H^nK)$ and $c_L^n:H^n(FL)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H^nL)$ satisfying $c_L^n\circ H^n(Fs)=F(H^n s)\circ c_K^n$. These are the precise cohomology comparisons needed; no assumption on coproduct preservation by $F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, degreewise kernel/cokernel comparison; as packaged by the cited existing cohomology lemma

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every $H^n(s)$ is invertible. A functor preserves an inverse: $F((H^n s)^{-1})$ is inverse to $F(H^n s)$ by the composition and identity axioms. The comparison equation of the preceding step then writes $H^n(Fs)=(c_L^n)^{-1}\circ F(H^n s)\circ c_K^n$, a composite of isomorphisms. Thus $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree. Restricting $s$ to morphisms between two K-flat complexes gives exactly the required preservation property; it does not assert that $F(P)$ itself is K-flat, and no tensor structure on $\mathcal D$ is required.
